m: of or relating to a style of furniture developed in Germany in the 19th century
transitional period between Neoclassicism and Romanticism as it was interpreted by the bourgeoisie, particularly in Germany, Austria, northern Italy, and the Scandinavian countries.
In general, the Biedermeier style offered visual evidence of the conflict of ideas between Classicism and Romanticism that continued during the first half of the 19th century.
having a life cycle lasting two seasons
(botany) a plant having a life cycle that normally takes two seasons from germination to death to complete; flowering biennials usually bloom and fruit in the second season
a coffin along with its stand
we followed the bier to the graveyard
a stand to support a corpse or a coffin prior to burial
